19@pointwise_dynamic(promotion_methods=[(0, "INT_TO_FLOAT")]) 

20@triton.jit 

21def tanh_kernel(x): 

22 return _tanh(x.to(tl.float32))

25@pointwise_dynamic(promotion_methods=[(0, "INT_TO_FLOAT")]) 

26@triton.jit 

27def tanh_backward_kernel(y, dy): 

28 y = y.to(tl.float32) 

29 return dy.to(tl.float32) * (1.0 - y * y)

31 

32# -------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

33# tanh_backward flat stride-1 fast path (2026-09-09, harness/solution/tanh_backward) 

34# 

35# Why: `tanh_backward_kernel` above is a bare `pointwise_dynamic` with **no 

36# `config=`**, so it inherits the kunlunxin default `CodeGenConfig(512, ...)` 

37# from `_kunlunxin/utils/codegen_config_utils.py` (max_tile_size=512, 

38# `unroll_num=0`, `buffer_size_limit=0`). Measured cost of that path (shared 

39# card, us per call, `harness/solution/tanh_backward/micro_ab.py`): 

40# 

41# n vendor kernel generic pointwise_dynamic 

42# 1K .. 1M 19 .. 22 us 107 .. 110 us <- fixed host-side cost 

43# 16.7M (fp16) 75 us 162 us (~610 GB/s) 

44# 67.1M (fp16) 242 us 334 us (~1190 GB/s) 

45# 

46# So the generic path pays a ~107 us floor **per call** that is independent of 

47# size: eight of the twelve benchmark shapes are <=4M elements and are therefore 

48# 5x slower than the vendor kernel purely from dispatch overhead, before any 

49# memory traffic. A flat stride-1 kernel launched directly cuts that floor to 

50# ~37-50 us. 

51# 

52# in_grad = dy * (1 - y*y) is pure pointwise, two inputs / one output, no 

53# reduction and no `tl.where` (HARNESS_SUMMARY section 4.0: `tl.where` is the 

54# most expensive primitive on this backend, so none is introduced). The fp32 

55# expression below is written in exactly the same order as 

56# `tanh_backward_kernel`, so the fast path is bit-identical to the generic path 

57# for every dtype. 

58# 

59# Access shape is identical to `atan2` after its select-free rewrite (2 loads + 

60# 1 store, stride-1, memory bound), so the launch options are taken from 

61# `atan2.py`. The **tile policy is not** -- `atan2`'s 2048/8192 buckets were 

62# re-measured here and are far off optimum for this shape ladder; see the sweep 

63# below. 

64# 

65# Tile sweep (2026-09-09, shared card, us/call, 2 loads + 1 store, all three 

66# float dtypes; `harness/solution/tanh_backward/sweep_ladder.py`). BLOCK is the 

67# only variable that matters: `num_warps` 8/16/32, `unroll_num` 8/16/32 and 

68# `buffer_size_limit` 8192/16384 all land inside +-1% of each other. 

69# 

70# fp16 16.7M : 2048 514 4096 307 8192 190 16384 137 32768 117 65536 112 

71# bf16 16.7M : 2048 573 4096 328 8192 215 16384 173 32768 145 65536 134 

72# fp32 16.7M : 2048 540 4096 292 8192 195 16384 181 32768 167 65536 158 

73# fp16 67.1M : 2048 1939 4096 1041 8192 582 16384 390 32768 312 65536 284 

74# fp16 262K : 8192 55 16384 42 32768 48 65536 50 

75# fp16 4096 : 2048 58 4096 61 8192 59 16384 54 32768 53 65536 193 

76# 

77# => three buckets: <=16K -> 2048 (launch-floor bound, ~50 us for every tile 

78# width, so take the narrowest and waste no lanes), <=1M -> 16384, above -> 65536. 

79# The 8192-lane tile `atan2` uses would have **regressed** the four >=16.7M cases 

80# of the benchmark matrix against the generic path (fp16 67.1M: 582 us vs the 

81# generic path's 421 us); that regression is exactly what the sweep found and 

82# removed. 

83# 

84# Tile width stops at 65536 on purpose. HARNESS_SUMMARY section 3 records 

85# `tl.store(bf16_ptr, fp32_val.to(tl.bfloat16))` hanging a whole card at 

86# TILE=131072, and section 3.1 records a 32768-lane unmasked tile doing the same 

87# in `special_ndtr`. 65536 was therefore stepped up one width at a time under 

88# `timeout`, tiny grid first, and has since run the full 12-shape x 3-dtype 

89# ladder plus the equivalence and test suites clean. Note also that dropping 

90# `buffer_size_limit` (i.e. the backend default `buffer_size_limit=0, 

91# unroll_num=0`) makes even BLOCK=8192 fail to compile with 

92# `triton.runtime.errors.OutOfResources: out of resource: uni_sram` -- the 

93# bounded SRAM buffer is what makes the wide tiles legal at all. 

94# 

95# GEMS_KUNLUNXIN_TANH_BACKWARD_LEGACY=1 forces the original 

96# `pointwise_dynamic` path. This is the one-constant arm switch of 

97# HARNESS_SUMMARY section 6.7: it lets the BASE and POST benchmark arms run 

98# back-to-back inside a single exclusive card claim (exclusive windows on this 

99# machine are minutes long at best) instead of relying on a source checkout 

100# between arms. Default (unset) is the fast path. 

101# -------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

102_LEGACY_TANH_BACKWARD = os.environ.get("GEMS_KUNLUNXIN_TANH_BACKWARD_LEGACY") == "1" 

103 

104_FAST_DTYPES = (torch.float16, torch.float32, torch.bfloat16) 

105UNROLL_NUM = 16 

106BUFFER_SIZE_LIMIT = 8192 

107IS_CLOSE_MEMORY_ASYNC = False 

108 

109# bf16 upper bound for the fast path (2026-09-09, 

110# `harness/solution/tanh_backward/bf16_crossover.py`, us/call, spread over three 

111# repeats < 1%): 

112# 

113# n bf16 fast bf16 generic | fp16 fast fp16 generic 

114# 8 Mi 91 133 | 65 128 

115# 16 Mi 124 163 | 94 157 

116# 32 Mi 202 221 | 149 213 

117# 64 Mi 363 339 | 262 328 

118# 

119# Same byte traffic as fp16, but bf16 costs ~35 % more in the flat kernel: the 

120# `fp32 -> bf16` store conversion, not memory, is the limit there, and past 

121# 32 Mi elements the generic `pointwise_dynamic` path wins. So bf16 above 

122# 32 Mi keeps the generic path -- this is a bucketing decision between two XPU 

123# Triton kernels, no host/ATen fallback. The obvious "just widen the tile" 

124# answer is not available: HARNESS_SUMMARY section 3 records exactly 

125# `tl.store(bf16_ptr, fp32_val.to(tl.bfloat16))` at TILE=131072 hanging a card. 

126_BF16_FAST_MAX_NUMEL = 32 << 20 

127 

128 

129def _pick_block(n_elements): 

130 # Three buckets only -> at most 6 compiled variants (masked/unmasked x 3 

131 # tiles) per dtype, so the compile cost stays bounded. Boundaries and widths 

132 # come from the sweep table in the header comment. 

133 if n_elements <= 16384: 

134 return 2048, 4, n_elements % 2048 != 0 

135 if n_elements <= 1048576: 

136 return 16384, 8, n_elements % 16384 != 0 

137 return 65536, 8, n_elements % 65536 != 0 

138 

139 

140@triton.jit 

141def tanh_backward_flat_kernel(y_ptr, dy_ptr, out_ptr, n_elements, BLOCK: tl.constexpr): 

142 pid = ext.program_id(0) 

143 offs = pid * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK) 

144 mask = offs < n_elements 

145 y = tl.load(y_ptr + offs, mask=mask, other=0).to(tl.float32) 

146 dy = tl.load(dy_ptr + offs, mask=mask, other=0).to(tl.float32) 

147 res = dy * (1.0 - y * y) 

148 tl.store(out_ptr + offs, res.to(out_ptr.dtype.element_ty), mask=mask) 

149 

150 

151@triton.jit 

152def tanh_backward_flat_kernel_unmasked(y_ptr, dy_ptr, out_ptr, BLOCK: tl.constexpr): 

153 pid = ext.program_id(0) 

154 offs = pid * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK) 

155 y = tl.load(y_ptr + offs).to(tl.float32) 

156 dy = tl.load(dy_ptr + offs).to(tl.float32) 

157 res = dy * (1.0 - y * y) 

158 tl.store(out_ptr + offs, res.to(out_ptr.dtype.element_ty))

161def _tanh_backward_fast_eligible(grad_output, output): 

162 if _LEGACY_TANH_BACKWARD: 

163 return False 

164 if not (torch.is_tensor(grad_output) and torch.is_tensor(output)): 

165 return False 

166 if output.dtype is not grad_output.dtype or output.dtype not in _FAST_DTYPES: 

167 return False 

168 if output.shape != grad_output.shape: 

169 return False 

170 # 0-dim tensors go to the generic path (one element, launch bound anyway). 

171 if output.dim() == 0 or output.numel() == 0: 

172 return False 

173 if output.dtype is torch.bfloat16 and output.numel() > _BF16_FAST_MAX_NUMEL: 

174 return False 

175 return output.is_contiguous() and grad_output.is_contiguous() 

176 

177 

178def _tanh_backward_fast(grad_output, output): 

179 n_elements = output.numel() 

180 out = torch.empty_like(output) 

181 block, warps, masked = _pick_block(n_elements) 

182 with bf16_fast_store(out.dtype): 

183 if masked: 

184 grid = (triton.cdiv(n_elements, block),) 

185 tanh_backward_flat_kernel[grid]( 

186 output, 

187 grad_output, 

188 out, 

189 n_elements, 

190 BLOCK=block, 

191 num_warps=warps, 

192 unroll_num=UNROLL_NUM, 

193 buffer_size_limit=BUFFER_SIZE_LIMIT, 

194 isCloseMemoryAsync=IS_CLOSE_MEMORY_ASYNC, 

195 ) 

196 else: 

197 grid = (n_elements // block,) 

198 tanh_backward_flat_kernel_unmasked[grid]( 

199 output, 

200 grad_output, 

201 out, 

202 BLOCK=block, 

203 num_warps=warps, 

204 unroll_num=UNROLL_NUM, 

205 buffer_size_limit=BUFFER_SIZE_LIMIT, 

206 isCloseMemoryAsync=IS_CLOSE_MEMORY_ASYNC, 

207 ) 

208 return out

211def tanh(self): 

212 logger.debug("GEMS_KUNLUNXIN TANH") 

213 out = tanh_kernel(self) 

214 return out

217def tanh_backward(grad_output, output): 

218 logger.debug("GEMS_KUNLUNXIN TANH_BACKWARD") 

219 if _tanh_backward_fast_eligible(grad_output, output): 

220 return _tanh_backward_fast(grad_output, output) 

221 in_grad = tanh_backward_kernel(output, grad_output) 

222 return in_grad
